title: A report in numbered sections, each a titled table with its total row and a line on what it shows
about: A board or month-end report, a summary for someone who asked for named parts ('1 Visits by month', '2 Open tickets by age'): each section its own query, drawn as a table in the order given, numbered, with a total row over the columns named in its total, and a note under it that explains it (why the first period has no change, what is left out). Choose it whenever the request names the parts of a report or asks for it to read like a report rather than a dashboard.

sections.about: the sections in order: [{"title", "query" (a SELECT, :today is the day), "columns": [{"key", "label", "format": money | number | date | text}], "total": [column keys summed in a total row], "note"}], up to 8

sub.about: a line under the heading (the period it covers)

sections.title: Visits by month
sections.query: SELECT month, SUM(visits) AS visits FROM traffic GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
sections.note: Each visit counted in the month it was made.

sections.title: Open tickets by days open
sections.query: SELECT band_of(days_between(opened, :today)) AS band, MIN(band_rank(days_between(opened, :today))) AS r, COUNT(*) AS tickets FROM tickets WHERE status = 'open' GROUP BY band_of(days_between(opened, :today)) ORDER BY r

let.{{key}}_secs: ={{sections|json}}.slice(0, 8).map((s, i) => { const rows = data[{{key|json}} + '_' + (i + 1)] || []; const cols = s.columns && s.columns.length ? s.columns : Object.keys(rows[0] || {}).filter(k => k !== 'id').map(k => ({key: k})); return {n: i + 1, title: s.title, note: s.note || null, cols: cols.map(c => ({key: c.key, label: c.label || c.key, format: c.format || null})), rows, total: Array.isArray(s.total) && s.total.length ? s.total : false}; })
